sources.content: Spec JQ-48: prorated plan upgrades in Jornquil Billing. Today, a customer who upgrades mid-cycle pays the full price of the new plan at the next renewal and gets nothing back for the unused days of the old plan. This spec charges the price difference right away, prorated by the days left in the cycle. The charge is computed in cents and rounded down. Downgrades are not prorated; they take effect at the next renewal. Annual plans are in scope. The spec owner is the Billing Platform team.

Limits and rollout. A prorated charge under 50 cents is not charged right away; it is added to the next invoice instead. Proration uses the account's billing time zone, which defaults to UTC. The change ships behind the flag `billing.proration_v2`. Rollout starts with new accounts created after 2027-01-15, then moves existing accounts over in batches of 10,000 per day. Invoices issued before the switch are never recalculated. Success means a 20 percent drop in upgrade-related refund requests within two months.

claims.text: Under spec JQ-48, Jornquil prorates downgrades immediately.
Jornquil proration uses the account's billing time zone, which defaults to UTC.
Existing Jornquil accounts move to prorated upgrades in batches of 10,000 per day.
Prorated upgrade charges in Jornquil are computed in cents and rounded down.
Jornquil defers a prorated charge to the next invoice only when it is under 1 dollar.
The Jornquil proration change ships behind the flag billing.proration_v2.
